description:
A place to come when life is happening.
Life doesn’t always give us time to stop and process what we’re feeling.
Sometimes we’re overwhelmed. Sometimes we’re hurting. Sometimes we’re angry, confused, exhausted, hopeful, or simply trying to figure out what to do next.
These are slow, thoughtful audio reflections for those moments.
Each episode takes one of life’s real situations and sits with it gently — exploring the feelings we often struggle to put into words, the things we may not have considered, and the perspective we may need to move forward.
Some episodes are simply a place to breathe and remember what matters.
Rooted in Islamic values and thoughtful reflection, this is not about having all the answers or telling you to “fix your life.”
It’s about slowing down long enough to understand.
To find comfort when you need it.
To find courage when you need it.
To be challenged when you need it.
And sometimes, simply to know that you’re not the only one going through it.
Come as you are.
Put on your headphones.
Take a walk.

Or simply lie down and listen.
Whatever life is bringing you, there may be a place here for you.

The History of the Stock Market Podcast traces the exchanges, investors, companies, financial institutions, technologies, bubbles, crashes, and economic forces that transformed stock trading from informal deals between merchants into the enormous global financial system of today.

Episodes journey from the earliest joint-stock companies and the Amsterdam Stock Exchange through the rise of Wall Street, the New York Stock Exchange, famous market panics, the Great Crash of 1929, the Great Depression, postwar bull markets, the NASDAQ revolution, Black Monday, the dot-com bubble, the 2008 financial crisis, meme stocks, algorithmic trading, and the evolution of modern investing. The show also explores legendary investors, major corporations, financial scandals, regulation, short selling, market speculation, index funds, brokerage firms, trading technology, and the psychology behind booms and crashes.

Whether you are fascinated by Wall Street, investing, financial history, market crashes, legendary traders, economic bubbles, or the forces that have shaped modern capitalism, the podcast tells the stories behind the people, institutions, innovations, and defining moments that built the stock market. The History of the Stock Market Podcast is hosted by Josh Linsk.

title: חשופה
author: niv cohen
description:
בואו נדבר על מה שבאמת קורה בינינו.
על אהבה. על תשוקה. על משיכה. על גברים. על נשים. על סקס. על פרידות. על בגידות. על הלב שנשבר, על האגו שנפגע, על ההודעות שאנחנו מנתחות עם חברות ועל כל הפעמים שאנחנו יודעות שמישהו לא נכון לנו — ועדיין לא מצליחות לשחרר.
ב״חשופה״ אין פילטרים ואין מסכות.
יש אמת.
גם כשהיא כואבת. גם כשהיא לא נוחה. וגם כשהיא גורמת לנו לשאול את עצמנו שאלות שלא תמיד רצינו לשאול.
אני יהודית גאולייב, מנטורית לזוגיות ומחברת הספר ״חשופה״, ובכל פרק אני נכנסת יחד איתכם למקומות הכי רגישים, מסקרנים ולפעמים גם אסורים של מערכות יחסים.
נדבר על מה נשים באמת רוצות מגברים ומה גברים באמת מחפשים בנשים. למה אנחנו נמשכים דווקא למי שלא נותן לנו את מה שאנחנו צריכים. למה לפעמים דווקא כשמישהו רוצה אותנו — אנחנו מאבדים עניין. מה גורם למשיכה להידלק ומה מכבה אותה. למה אנשים בוגדים. למה אנחנו נשארים בקשרים שכבר מזמן היו צריכים להיגמר. ואיך לעזאזל יודעים שזו באמת אהבה — ולא עוד דפוס בתחפושת.
יהיו כאן נשים. יהיו כאן גברים. יהיו סיפורים אמיתיים, דעות שלא תמיד נסכים עליהן, שאלות שלא תמיד נעים לשאול ותשובות שלא תמיד קל לשמוע.
ובעיקר — נדבר אמת.
כי מתחת לכל המשחקים, החוקים, האסטרטגיות והחיפוש אחרי ״האחד״ או ״האחת״, נמצאת מערכת היחסים שממנה הכול מתחיל:
מערכת היחסים שלנו עם עצמנו.
וכשאנחנו מפסיקים לפחד להסתכל פנימה, אנחנו מתחילים לבחור אחרת גם בחוץ.
חשופה.על אהבה, תשוקה, נשים, גברים וכל מה שקורה ביניהם כשאף אחד לא מסתכל.
בלי פילטרים. בלי מסכות. בלי בולשיט.

description: True Crime Podcast, for mature audiences. Buried, Not Forgotten is about the mysterious deaths of Walter Smith and Peter Hauer, in the summer of 1975. Smith never returned from a bike ride from his summer job at Watoga State Park in Pocahontas County, West Virginia. A large-scale search was initiated that week, and volunteer cavers and West Virginia State Police would eventually discover Walter Smith’s body in a cave, under a pile of rocks, on private property. The property owner, Peter Hauer, was a leading expert on saltpeter mining, an accomplished cave explorer, historian and treasurer of the American Spelean History Association. Hauer went missing that same week, shortly after being interviewed by investigators. Some people believe the story in the police report; Peter killed Walter, then took his own life, but many friends and neighbors refuse to believe that is what really happened. In the course of the project, Buried Not Forgotten uncovered information about the police report, FBI investigation, and first-hand accounts that paint a very different picture from what police believed in 1975. Listen to those closest to the case, in their own words, as the truth gets even stranger than it seems at first.

title: Back Garden Cricket Club
author: Back Garden Cricket Club
description:
Back garden cricket has its own laws: unwritten, fiercely argued, and unique to every lawn, patio and flowerbed in the land. Nobody has ever written them down. Until now.

Forty years ago, the legendary "Whisperin'" Bob Harris and Jon Briggs, the original voice of Siri, played cricket in Bob's back garden. Most of the players turned up for the fun, and for the magnificent teas. Bob took it rather more seriously. He kept every score and worked out everyone's averages, and he still has them.

Finding those scorebooks brought the memories flooding back, along with the gloriously bizarre rules needed to make cricket work in Bob's garden. So Bob and Jon have set out to compile the laws the MCC somehow forgot to catalogue.

With the help of some brilliant professional cricketers, they're going back to where it all began: "one hand, one bounce", "tip and run" and the rest. After all, no first-class cricketer started out at Lord's or the MCG. They started with a watering can for a wicket and a healthy fear of the rule that a six over next door's fence means you're out.

Pads on. Welcome to the Back Garden Cricket Club.

Welcome to Gran Sleep History.

​Every week, we guide you through the chaos of the digital landscape. We cover everything from avoiding algorithm obsolescence and commanding premium rates with AI skills, to navigating the wild, high-conversion world of live social commerce. We also translate boring bureaucratic nightmares,
 ​Whether you're trying to dodge "VIP task" scams on Telegram, figuring out zero-commission freelance platforms, or just trying to remember to pay your voluntary social security, we are your ultimate survival guide to the digital rat race. Put some pants on (or don't), upskill yourself, and tune in!

title: The Debrief by Power Up Church

description:
The Mission Briefing happens Sunday. The Debrief happens Monday.

Every week, Fleet Commander Brandon Holm delivers the Mission Briefing in the Ready Room — the teaching gathering of Power Up Church, a future-focused, nerd-native church reaching believers, seekers, skeptics, and anyone who never fit the traditional church mold, in more than 25 countries. The next day, hosts Erin Dunn and Patrick Nash open the after-action report: a genuine conversation that unpacks the briefing, chases down its tensions, works through the Scripture at its center, and presses on what the teaching actually means for the crew's faith, character, and mission capacity.

This is not a rerun of the sermon audio. It is the debrief that follows the mission — what challenged us, what held up, and what we're each carrying into the week ahead.

New episodes land Monday 17:00 America/Phoenix (Tuesday 09:00 JST).

Erin Dunn and Patrick Nash are virtual hosts --- AI-assisted personas created by Power Up Church for The Debrief. Every Mission Briefing they review is delivered by Fleet Commander Brandon Holm, a real, ordained minister. The theology on this show comes from Scripture and the teaching ministry of real people; Erin and Patrick are the medium, not the source.

If these after-action reports sharpen your thinking, follow The Debrief by Power Up Church on your podcast app of choice --- Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or your preferred player --- so every new episode lands automatically.

From AI and the future of education to inflation, trade wars, innovation, data, sustainability, marketing, democracy and inequality, each episode starts with a simple question and goes deeper, connecting academic research with the issues shaping our everyday lives.

No lectures. No easy answers. Just students and professors exchanging ideas and looking at the world from different perspectives.

Take a break. Stay curious.

Because surgery is only the start of the story. It’s what happens next that matters most.

What the City Has to Say...

Forget the postcard. The lights, the casinos, the Strip, that's the ten-second version of Vegas, built for people who are just passing through. Behind it is a real city of nearly two and a half million people building businesses, raising kids, making art, chasing ideas, taking hits and getting back up. This show hands them the mic.

Listen Vegas is hosted and produced right here in Las Vegas, no outside crew, no tourist lens. Every episode is an honest, unscripted conversation with business owners, artists, longtime locals, and everyday residents about what it actually takes to live, work, and build a life in one of the most misunderstood cities in the country.

No club guides. No buffet reviews. No fake hype pretending everything here is a party. Just real people telling real stories about the Vegas that exists after the tourists go home.

If you were born here, moved here, built something here, or you're still trying to figure this city out, this show is for you. Because there's another Las Vegas underneath the one on the boulevard, and it's louder, realer, and far more interesting than anything on a billboard.

description:
A home is more than a place to live it’s where everyday moments happen. From enjoying a quiet morning with a cup of coffee to spending time with family after a long day, the furniture around you becomes part of those experiences. That's why choosing the right furniture isn't simply about filling a room. It's about creating a space that feels comfortable, practical, and welcoming.

While many people are tempted to buy furniture based only on price, quality should always be part of the decision. Well-crafted furniture doesn't just look better it performs better, lasts longer, and continues to add value to your home year after year. http://houseoffurnishes.co.uk

Furniture Shapes the Way You Live

Furniture Shapes the Way You Live Every room has a purpose, and the furniture you choose helps define that purpose. Think about your favourite place at home. It might be the lounge chair where you relax after work or the dining table where everyone gathers for dinner. These aren't just pieces of furniture they're part of your daily routine. Choosing furniture that supports your lifestyle makes everyday living more enjoyable.

What Defines High-Quality Furniture?

Not all furniture is built to the same standard. Quality furniture is designed with durability, comfort, and craftsmanship in mind. Instead of focusing only on appearance, it combines premium materials with thoughtful construction. Some features worth looking for include:
  • Solid and stable frames
  • Carefully finished surfaces
  • Comfortable cushioning
  • Durable upholstery
  • Strong joints and reliable construction
These details may seem small, but they make a significant difference over time.

Why Designer Chairs Continue to Stand Out

Designer chairs have earned their reputation because they combine function with timeless beauty. Rather than following temporary trends, these chairs are created with balanced proportions, clean lines, and lasting comfort. Whether placed in a living room, office, or reading corner, they naturally become a focal point without overwhelming the space. A well-designed chair can provide:
  • Comfortable everyday seating
  • Elegant visual appeal
  • Long-lasting durability
  • Easy integration with different décor styles
It's this combination that keeps designer-inspired furniture popular generation after generation.

Choosing Furniture That Fits Your Lifestyle

Every household has different needs. Before purchasing new furniture, take a moment to think about how you'll actually use it. Ask yourself:
  • Will this be used every day?
  • Is it suitable for my available space?
  • Does it offer enough comfort?
  • Will it complement my existing décor?
  • Is it built for long-term use?
These questions often lead to smarter purchasing decisions.

Final Thoughts

Quality furniture is about more than appearance. It supports your daily routine, improves comfort, and helps create spaces where people enjoy spending time together. Choosing well-crafted designer chairs and timeless furniture means investing in pieces that continue to perform beautifully long after passing trends have disappeared. By focusing on craftsmanship, durable materials, and practical design, you create interiors that remain welcoming, functional, and stylish for many years.

title: The Scrolls Of Reflection
author: Zaib Shamsi
description:
Welcome to The Scrolls of Reflection, a weekly exploration of engineering, human systems, resilience, ambition, failure, reinvention and the lessons that emerge when life refuses to follow the path you originally designed.
 
Hosted by Zaib Shamsi, a Biomedical Engineering MSc graduate from the University of Liverpool with an extensive background in applied medical sciences and healthcare, The Scrolls of Reflection brings together two very different chapters of one journey. Before moving into biomedical engineering, Zaib developed an extensive academic and healthcare background spanning more than five years, earning a BSc in Applied Medical Sciences and developing an understanding of the human body, disease, clinical reasoning and healthcare. Personal circumstances led him to transition away from that pathway, relocate to Liverpool and begin building a different future.
 
That transition became the beginning of a new chapter.
 
Over the following year at the University of Liverpool, biomedical engineering provided a different way of looking at problems that had once been approached primarily through applied medical sciences and healthcare. Engineering introduced another perspective: understanding complex systems, analysing data, designing solutions, experimenting with technology and examining how biological and technical systems interact. The experience became about considerably more than completing a Master’s degree. It represented rebuilding direction after years invested in another path and learning how knowledge from one chapter can be carried forward into something entirely different.

The Scrolls of Reflection is built around what those six years taught him.

Each episode unfolds as a new “Scroll”: a focused reflection examining an idea, experience, system or lesson through the combined lenses of applied medical sciences, biomedical engineering, systems thinking and lived experience.
 
Some Scrolls explore the architecture of human performance: stress, resilience, adaptation, recovery and the limits of treating ourselves like machines. Others examine ambition, identity, failure, uncertainty, discipline, relationships, technology, engineering, personal infrastructure and the difficult process of rebuilding when the original plan disappears.
 
The podcast does not present life as a straightforward progression from failure to success. Instead, it explores the complicated territory between them: the periods where progress is difficult to recognise, where previous identities have to be reconsidered, where circumstances force adaptation and where apparent setbacks eventually become sources of knowledge.
 
Zaib draws upon more than half a decade of experience across applied medical sciences, healthcare and biomedical engineering to examine those questions from an unusual position: someone who has experienced healthcare through years of intensive study and practical exposure before subsequently approaching biological problems through engineering, experiments and analysis.
 
Alongside personal reflection, episodes explore the broader systems operating underneath everyday life. How does prolonged pressure affect human performance? What happens when ambition exceeds sustainable capacity? How can engineering principles change the way we understand biological problems? What does it mean to rebuild after investing years in one trajectory? How can failure become information rather than simply an endpoint? And how do we construct lives capable of adapting when circumstances change?
 
These are not stories about having everything figured out.
 
They are reflections produced by going through the process.
 
From more than five years immersed in applied medical sciences and healthcare, through a major personal and academic transition, to moving to Liverpool and completing an MSc in Biomedical Engineering (Healthcare) at the University of Liverpool, The Scrolls of Reflection documents the ideas, mistakes, discoveries and lessons accumulated across six transformative years.
 
Whether you are a student, engineer, healthcare professional, researcher, entrepreneur, high achiever or simply someone whose life has taken an unexpected direction, the Scrolls explore a central idea:
 
Your previous chapter does not become meaningless simply because you chose — or were forced — to write a different one.
 
Sometimes the knowledge acquired along the wrong path becomes part of the architecture required to build the right one.

description:

In this episode, Gene shares his own story: leaving school after the eighth grade, earning his GED days after Navy boot camp, and passing a make-or-break remedial algebra class at Richland Community College on the way to an associate's degree and, eventually, a doctorate.
Then he does the math:
- Time: a degree and a trade earned in the same two years.
- Money: Community college averaged about $4,150 a year in 2025-26, against about $11,950 at an in-state public university (College Board).
- Skills that multiply: why a tradesperson with a degree becomes the foreman, the estimator, or the owner.
- Compounding: why a four-year head start keeps paying for the rest of a life.
He also explains the legal roads a teenager can take today, including dual enrollment and early college high schools, and why the old road can cost six years, whereas the new one takes two.

He is hunted, after all, by a procession of manic apparitions stepping out from his regret-filled past, and the grotesque and gargantuan insect god that feeds on them: “The Silverfish.” To blaze any trail home, Remmy will have to rip a paradox apart and use the pieces to forge an answer to an unanswerable question: how do you out-think a god who eats your very thoughts?

This is Radical Buddhism , where Ryan Lee Wong, author and former Zen monastic, talks to Asian American Buddhist leaders about the relationship between inner change and social change, faith and politics. Together, they’ll explore how the Buddha’s teachings of 2,500 years offer us the rituals, insights, and skills to build a more compassionate society.
Radical Buddhism is a production of Axis Mundi Media ( https://www.axismundi.us/ ) , made possible by a grant from the Henry Luce Foundation, which seeks to deepen public knowledge of religion. title: Blessed By Golf
author: Ian Butler
description:
Blessed by Golf — The Stories Behind the Game
Golf gives us a lot more than a scorecard.
It gives us friendships. Opportunities. Mentors. Careers. Confidence. Second chances. Competition. Community. And sometimes, it puts people in our lives who change our direction completely.
Blessed by Golf is about those stories.
We're not here to break down tour statistics, debate rankings, review the newest equipment, or tell you how to fix your swing. There are plenty of great places to find that.
We want to know something different:
What has golf given you?
Every golfer has a story. Maybe the game introduced you to your best friend or your spouse. Maybe a relationship built on a golf course opened a door in your career. Maybe golf gave you something to hold onto during a difficult time, brought you back to something you'd given up on, or taught you lessons about patience, resilience, trust and perseverance that followed you far beyond the course.
Those are the stories we want to tell.
Through conversations with golfers, athletes, business leaders, professionals, personalities and everyday people who simply love the game, Blessed by Golf explores the people, relationships and moments that make golf about so much more than golf.
You'll also hear different voices and original series from within the Blessed by Golf family, each bringing their own experiences, guests and perspective — but always coming back to the same idea:
The best golf stories aren't always about golf. They're about what golf gives us.
And those stories have a purpose.
We collect them, share them with the world, and use the platform we're building to help create opportunities for the next generation to experience everything sports can give them.
Because long after you've forgotten the score, you'll remember the people you met, the places the game took you, and the moments that changed your life.
Blessed by Golf. The Stories Behind the Game.

title: Places remember
author: nigel higgins
description:
Places Remember

Every place has a story.

Mention the name of a village, a lonely stretch of coastline, a forgotten church, or a quiet woodland, and someone will remember something. It may be a family memory, a local legend, an event recorded in history, or simply a tale passed from one generation to the next.

Places become part of us. We celebrate there. We mourn there. We laugh, we fear, we love, and we leave pieces of ourselves behind. Long after the people have gone, the places remain, carrying the echoes of those who came before.

Perhaps that's why it sometimes feels as though places remember.

Not every memory is a happy one. Some tell of courage, kindness and hope. Others speak of tragedy, betrayal and loss. Some are firmly rooted in fact, while others have grown through years of whispered retellings, gathering new details with every passing generation until history and folklore become almost impossible to separate.

Places Remember explores those stories.

From forgotten crimes and remarkable lives to ghostly legends, strange happenings, curious folklore and the unexplained, each episode journeys into the memories attached to a place, not simply to ask what happened, but to discover how those stories have survived, changed and endured.

Because history is more than dates and documents. It lives in conversations, in family memories, in old newspaper cuttings, in weathered gravestones, in the names we still whisper, and in the landscapes that quietly bear witness to it all.

Whether the stories are true, embellished, or somewhere in between, they reveal something about the people who told them and the places that inspired them.

So join us as we visit the villages, coastlines, churches, forests and forgotten corners where memory lingers.

After all...

Every place remembers something.

Each episode bridges what a parent is carrying and what a baby is communicating. Topics cover what we, as clinicians, run into every day through our work with individuals in this period, alongside other professionals who specialize in these topics. 


We talk about matrescence, perinatal mental health conditions (PMHCs), attachment, co-regulation, responsive caregiving, and the postpartum months nobody prepares you for. It's a reflective lens holding space for both parent and infant to be seen as individuals and as a unit. All in language you can actually use.


If you're a parent, these are honest conversations that normalize the hard parts, make sense of your baby's behavior, and take the shame out of the days that feel like too much. If you're a clinician, birth worker, educator, home visitor, or early intervention provider, this podcast will provide relationship-based, reflective, culturally grounded practice you can carry into your next visit. 

Every family starts somewhere. These are the earliest relationships, the ones that teach a baby whether the world feels safe and teach a parent who they're becoming.

description:

I'm Erin Burt. I said yes, then I hung up the phone and panicked. Now I'm in my sixties, raising kids from my family, and I've stood on both sides of the door. I'm a kinship caregiver and a Reverse Empty Nester, and I'm still in it, come heck or high laundry.

Every week I share what I lived, what I learned, and where to go for help. We talk about the call that changes everything, trauma and big feelings, autism and sensory needs, the lasting effects of drug exposure, IEP meetings, burnout, and the moments of joy that make it all worth it.

I'm not a therapist, a social worker, or a lawyer. I'm a woman who has lived the questions you're asking right now. No judgment. Ever.

Pull up a chair. The porch light's on.

title: The Daily Strive

The Daily Strive is where I document what it actually takes to build a business on your own, no polish, no highlight reel.
19 years of coaching, owning a gym, and building (and failing at) multiple businesses along the way.
These days I call it Strivecta: the 3 forces [Power, Precision, and Profit] that pull at every solopreneur at once.
This show is the real, unedited version of working through it every day.
Connect with me on Instagram: @coachstian or check out coachstian.com

title: Divinely Inspired Business Podcast
author: Kelly and Evan Mimier
description: Divinely Inspired Business explores the faith, mindset, intuition, perseverance, and unexpected moments behind extraordinary entrepreneurial stories. Hosted by husband-and-wife entrepreneurs Kelly and Evan Mimier, the podcast features conversations with people from all walks of life who followed an idea, took a leap, pushed through uncertainty, and built something they once weren’t sure was possible. Some call it God. Some call it intuition. Others describe manifestation, synchronicity, instinct, preparation, luck, or simply refusing to give up. We’re curious about all of it.

description:
Welcome to Coffee, Chaos and Cussing—the podcast for moms who love their kids like crazy but occasionally need five damn minutes away from them.
Motherhood is beautiful, exhausting, hilarious, overwhelming, and sometimes completely fucking unhinged. Here, we’re talking about the real stuff: marriage, kids, mental load, mom guilt, friendships, work, sex, self-care, school chaos, and all the things we think but don’t always say out loud.
And because moms don’t actually get alone time—we get hiding time—every episode comes to you from wherever we’re hiding: the bathroom, the closet, the car, the

With experience in both chiropractic care and nursing, she takes a well-rounded approach to health. Jade Guerra focuses on spine care, preventing injuries, and improving her patients' overall quality of life. She works closely with each person to create care plans that meet their unique needs.

title: ZNO Industry Deepdive - Zochem AI
author: Zochem
description:
Have you ever wondered how zinc oxide is used to create so many things, from your daily sunscreen and tires to electronics and batteries? Welcome to ZNO Industry Deepdive, the AI-powered podcast from Zochem that simplifies the science, innovation, and everyday impact of zinc oxide, one of the world's most versatile materials.

In each episode, we take heavy technical concepts and turn them into clear, conversational deep dives. Whether you are an industry professional, a curious student, or someone who loves knowing how things work, we translate complex chemistry into engaging, easily digestible stories.

title: Disability is my Strength - The Podcast
author: Vicki Wilson
description:
Tired of disability being talked about as either tragedy or inspiration?
Disability Is My Strength is about the bit in between. Real life, real challenges, big ambitions and the assumptions people make along the way.
I’m Vicki Wilson, a disabled business owner, author and speaker living with cerebral palsy. Through solo episodes and guest conversations, we’ll talk about disability, confidence, inclusion, resilience, business and what it really means to create your own version of what is possible.
This isn’t about pretending barriers do not exist. It is about questioning the ones other people put in front of us and having honest conversations about how we move forward.
Expect personal stories, thought-provoking guests and plenty of straight-talking, with new episodes released regularly.

title: This Could Go Viral
author: Libby de Leon
description:
This Could Go Viral is the podcast for you.
If you’re a 90s kid or Gen Z, you didn’t just grow up on the internet, t he internet grew up with you.
From internet nostalgia, to algorithm changes to side hustles that accidentally become careers, This Could Go Viral is the playbook for navigating life on the internet.
You’re doomscrolling anyway.
You might as well make a little money off it.

title: Kristi Muzzio
author: Kristi Muzzio
description: Kristi Muzzio is an accomplished opera singer and voice educator with a career rooted in performance, scholarship, and teaching. She holds a Doctor of Arts in Voice Performance and Pedagogy and advanced vocology training. Kristi has appeared in principal operatic roles and orchestral performances across the United States while focusing her work on vocal wellness, expressive artistry, student development, and expanding opera education through mentorship, research, performance leadership, and regional community engagement initiatives nationwide.

title: The Last Straw Podcast
author: Kristi Straw
description:
High achievers hit a breaking point. The world calls it burnout. We call it a reckoning.


The Last Straw is where executive women, founders, and quiet disruptors finally get the truth about leadership, identity, and the visibility required to grow your influence and your income. This is where the polished stage meets the real story. The boardroom meets the breakdown and rebuild. The ambition gets a voice.


Each episode pulls you behind the scenes of what actually happens after the keynote, inside high stakes rooms, and in the private moments leaders never talk about. You’ll hear the conversations clients whisper after the promotion. The fears that surface before the opportunity. The power moves that change everything.


Visibility becomes capital here. Presence becomes strategy. Voice becomes the asset that sets your career, your business, and your legacy on a different trajectory.


This is your entry point into the Lighthouse Leadership ecosystem. If you’re craving clarity, identity-led authority, and real elevation, you’re in the right place.


You’ll leave every episode feeling seen, activated, and a little giddy you found us.


Subscribe and step into the room.

title: Purity Bay
author: Elemental Gaming nexus
description:
Welcome ot Purity Bay! It ain't so pure. It ain't much of a bay. 

That’s Redacted is an actual-play Delta Green podcast. This campaign takes place in the homebrewed fictional town of Purity Bay, Illinois. 
In 1964, five towns became one county. About ten thousand people, dirt roads, one highway, a Walmart that ate the shops on the Main Streets, and a toy factory dumping pollution into the air. Surrounding it all is The Bed: a dead lake full of stranded ships, land races, and things people do where the lights do not reach. Deputy Jaime Prospero just came down from Chicago trying to make it to detective. Deputy Tim Brown has lived here his whole life and wants to keep the town safe. Florian Carter grew up getting shoved around by the same families, made it out, and has returned to do some method acting. A body on Buckberry Farm kicks off an investigation that will take us into the darkness of Purity Bay. 

You can expect serious moments, bad jokes and a whole lot of unantrual horror. Bonds will be damaged, lives will be lost and just maybe the Bay can be saved.

Stay ahead of the threats that matter most. Each week, Logica Security brings you a concise executive briefing on the latest developments in cyber, information and physical security — and what they mean for your business.

From major breaches to new laws and emerging technologies, you’ll hear what’s happening, why it matters, and the key questions every leader should be asking inside their organisation.

Because resilience starts in the boardroom.

title: The Ink Stays Dark
author: Adrian Klein
description:
The Ink Stays Dark explores the moral questions beneath crime, silence, memory, power, and the stories people try to control.

Hosted by writer Adrian Klein, the podcast moves through real cases, history, psychology, institutions, and fiction to examine what people do when truth becomes expensive.

Why do good people stay silent?

Why do some stories disappear while others refuse to stay buried?

What happens in the moments before a decision becomes visible?

The Ink Stays Dark began in psychological noir, but now follows the human pressure underneath it: witnesses, records, family secrets, corruption, responsibility, and the quiet choices that shape public truth.

For listeners drawn to moral ambiguity, institutional failure, memory, European noir, and the darker questions beneath ordinary life.

New episodes biweekly.

In the Company of Charity is a podcast that invites listeners into meaningful conversations about the Catholic Church, society, and service to others, all through the lens of the spirit we've received from St. Vincent de Paul, the saint of charity. We explore how the spirit of service can inspire real-world action and personal transformation. Whether you're seeking spiritual enrichment or a deeper understanding of charitable work, you'll find companionship and insight here.

Join in the conversation by sending us your thoughts and questions at companyofcharity@gmail.com.

title: The Vanguard Wall Podcast
author: The Vanguard Wall Podcast
description:
Long-form interviews with combat veterans, special operators, and first responders — the people who did the hard things and carry them home. The host, an Army and law-enforcement veteran, goes deep on the moments most podcasts skip: the call made under fire, the teammate lost, and the long quiet work of putting it back together. Guests include Green Berets, Rangers, Delta, MACV-SOG, CIA, pilots, and police — plus founders, filmmakers, and voices in health and resilience. For warriors, and the families who love them. New episodes every other week.
Contact: admin@thevanguardwall.com

title: I Heard You When You Said
author: Justin & Stacey
description:
You've read the books. You've done the therapy. You've tried the journaling, the meditation, the coping strategies. And you still feel it — that familiar weight, that loop you can't seem to break out of.


This podcast is for people who understand themselves really, really well and still keep running into the same walls. Hosted by mindset coaches Justin Carroll and Stacey Hansen, each episode gives you something you can actually do — not just something to think about.


Justin and Stacey work at the intersection of language, story, and the nervous system, and they've built their Fortified Mind Method around one simple truth: your body is still living in a story your brain has already tried to reason its way out of. Understanding why you're stuck doesn't unstick you. Moving through it does.

Every episode pulls back the curtain on real client breakthroughs, practical word games and exercises, and the kind of catchy sayings that stick with you because they're actually true. You'll leave each episode with something to write down, something to try, and someone in your life you'll want to share it with.


If history keeps rhyming for you — if you're tired of pushing things down instead of laying them down — you're in the right place.

title: Pleasure People
author: Danielle Bezalel
description: A thousand people. Three weeks. One question science rarely asks outright: what does daily pleasure actually do for you?   In this 6-part audio series, hosted by veteran sex educator Danielle Bezalel, Pleasure People follows eight participants of a first-of-its-kind intervention study that tracked pleasure's impact on sleep, stress, relationship satisfaction, and so much more. You'll hear directly from these participants about what it was like to have pleasure assigned and the lasting impact the study had on their lives. The findings will surprise you.  Danielle is joined by Magic Wand study lead researcher Dr. Candice Hargons and legendary sex researcher Emily Nagoski, Ph.D. to unpack the layered effect pleasure has on quality of life, and why self-pleasure has gotten such a bad rap.

title: What Now Then?
author: Jonathon Kelly
description:
What Now Then? is a podcast built around honest conversations with real people, real stories, and the moments in life that force us to stop and ask one simple question:

What now then?

Hosted by Jonathon Kelly in Western Australia, the podcast explores the turning points that shape who we become — the setbacks, breakthroughs, mistakes, relationships, challenges, losses, opportunities and unexpected changes that can completely alter the direction of a life.

This isn’t about pretending everybody has everything figured out.

It’s about what really happens behind the scenes.

Each episode brings a guest into a relaxed, genuine conversation about their life, their experiences and the lessons they’ve picked up along the way. Some guests may have achieved extraordinary things. Others may simply be ordinary people who have lived through extraordinary circumstances.

Either way, everybody has a story.

The conversations can move through relationships, recovery, mental health, family, personal growth, creativity, careers, business, purpose, success, failure and the difficult decisions we sometimes have to make when the life we expected doesn’t quite turn out the way we planned.

Because life rarely moves in a straight line.

Relationships change.

Careers change.

People change.

Plans fall apart.

Opportunities appear when we least expect them.

Sometimes we make the wrong decision. Sometimes we make the right decision and things still don’t work out. And sometimes the moments that feel like complete disasters at the time end up becoming the beginning of something entirely new.

Those are the moments What Now Then? is interested in.

This isn’t a traditional interview show built around rehearsed answers or carefully polished success stories. The goal is to create conversations that feel like you’re sitting in the room with us — curious, relaxed and willing to go wherever the discussion naturally leads.

There will be serious conversations.

There will be funny conversations.

There will probably be uncomfortable conversations.

And every now and again, we’ll disappear down a completely unexpected rabbit hole.

That’s part of it.

Jonathon isn’t sitting behind the microphone because he believes he has all the answers. The podcast exists because he still has plenty of questions.

What makes someone completely change direction?

How do people rebuild after things fall apart?

Why do some experiences stay with us for decades?

What have people learned about love, relationships, family, happiness, ambition and regret?

What does success actually mean once you’ve experienced it?

How do you know when it’s time to let something go?

And when everything changes…

What do you do next?

Sometimes one conversation can change the way you look at something.

Sometimes it’s a single story.

A mistake somebody admits to.

A lesson they learned the hard way.

Or one sentence that reaches you at exactly the right moment.

That’s what this podcast hopes to create.

Not perfect people.

Not perfect stories.

Just genuine human conversations about the experiences that make us who we are.

Season One marks the beginning of that journey — bringing together guests from different backgrounds, perspectives and walks of life, with each episode offering something new to think about.

So whether you’re rebuilding, changing direction, chasing something new, questioning where you’re heading, or you simply enjoy hearing fascinating people tell their stories, you’re invited to be part of the conversation.

title: This Wasn’t In The Brochure
author: thiswasntinthebrochure
description:
This Wasn’t in the Brochure: Because nobody prepared us for this shit.

Midlife was supposed to be the part where we finally had everything figured out.

Yeah… apparently not.

This Wasn’t in the Brochure is a podcast about the part of being a woman in midlife nobody really prepared us for—the hormones, the night sweats, the anxiety, the rage, the changing body, the changing relationships, the weird new relationship with alcohol, the kids needing us differently, and the unsettling realization that the life we spent decades building is changing.

But this isn’t a podcast about getting old.

It’s about figuring out what comes next.

I’m Abbigail Brown, and I’m right in the middle of it with you. I’m asking the questions, reading the research, talking to experts, trying the things everyone says will supposedly make our lives better—and reporting back on what actually works, what absolutely doesn’t, and what might be complete bullshit.

We’ll talk menopause, HRT, sleep, fitness, food, alcohol, mental health, marriage, friendships, money, purpose, aging, reinvention, and all the wellness crap suddenly being marketed to women our age.

And we’re going to try some shit, too.

New workouts. New hobbies. New places. Maybe meditation. Maybe surfing. Maybe salsa lessons. Maybe a retreat. Maybe something completely ridiculous.

Because somewhere between raising families, building careers, taking care of everyone else, and trying to remember why we walked into a room, a lot of us started asking the same question:

What do I actually want the rest of my life to look like?

I don't have the answer.

That's kind of the point.

Welcome to This Wasn’t in the Brochure.

Nobody prepared us for this shit.

So we might as well figure it out together.

title: Behind the Checkout

description: Behind the Checkout is an audiobook that explores the stories, strategies, psychology, and hidden business systems behind the things we buy every day.From a simple click on “Buy Now” to the product arriving at our doorstep, every purchase has a story behind it. Who sets the price? Why do we choose one product over another? How do discounts, free shipping, reviews, algorithms, and branding influence our decisions?Through everyday examples and easy-to-understand storytelling, Behind the Checkout takes you beyond the shopping cart to discover how e-commerce, consumer behavior, technology, and business shape the way we live.Because every purchase has a business story behind it.
